correctness.rationale: The 128 seven-bit edges of binary de Bruijn graph have 16 palindromic forbidden edges and 56 nonpalindromic reversal pairs. A valid necklace bijects with a directed closed trail containing at most one edge per reversal pair, and its distinct windows imply primitivity. Depth-first recursion from all eligible start states is exhaustive because each move marks a previously unused pair; crucially root revisits do not terminate extension. Two independently implemented exhaustive enumerations use different rooting rules. Independent compiled C++ search in this run reproduced all 29 positive-length table counts, total4788, maximal336, 90 symmetry orbits and all extremal local frequencies. This is an exhaustive finite proof for n=7 only, not a general theorem for other orders.
